bio: In the Ségala region, nestling in a village that is famous for its Cistercian church, this recently renovated little restaurant is accommodated in a half-timbered house. A well-travelled couple of industry professionals, Guilhem and Léonie, chef and pastry chef respectively, put a skilful spin on traditional fare such as shredded shoulder of lamb served tajine-style or, for dessert, citrus millefeuille with caramel and blood orange sorbet. The well-balanced and appealing menu they have come up with abounds with fresh and colourful dishes – plus it's excellent value for money. In short, they've got it all figured out. Delightful terrace laid out in the shade of an albizia and a magnolia....
